correctness.rationale: For a bounded positive independent quenched D, the reflection-principle erfc FPT formula holds exactly. K(0)>0 by strict Jensen, K tends to infinity due to positive mass above mean, and K is strictly convex because K'' is a strictly positive expectation. The CDF difference is negative near z=0 and positive for large z, so its derivative must be positive and K negative somewhere. Thus K has exactly two simple positive roots. The CDF derivative is a negative positive-multiple of K, yielding exactly one CDF zero, with correct temporal signs. Kernel curvature establishes the strict support bracket; uniform Taylor expansion establishes universal weak-disorder crossing limits. The independent symbolic/numerical checker passed 1,852 assertions on 185 representative laws; these are auxiliary finite checks, not the proof.

value.rationale: The exact global first-passage deadline comparison resolves whether quenched heterogeneity can alternate advantages repeatedly: it cannot, independent of arbitrary distribution shape. The two density crossings explain the mechanism and provide a nontrivial full-time classification; the strict support-only time bounds and universal weak-disorder limits give quantitative regimes relevant to heterogeneous first-arrival transport. The arbitrary-law structural conclusion and asymptotic positions are not just a textbook restatement of the known erfc mixture or an isolated numerical improvement.
